author: sltrib

item.caption:
From Washington City to Logan, Utahns showed up Saturday for the fourth nationwide “No Kings” day of protests — but this time, participants voted, too.

The demonstrations were meant to mobilize people to cast their midterm ballots early ahead of Election Day on Nov. 3, organizers said.

In Salt Lake City, protesters marched from the Capitol to a ballot drop box by Salt Lake City’s Main Library.

Around two thousand people gathered at the Capitol ahead of the march, filling the steps with American flags, protest signs, music and costumes — and a recurring message that change starts at the ballot box. Many in the crowd had already voted, but some who brought their ballots proudly waved them in the air.

🔗: Read more at the link in our bio.

(✍️: Samantha Moilanen | 📹: @LandwehrPhotography)

item.caption: 🚨 BALLOT INTEGRITY: California Outlaws Arrests Within 200 Feet of Polling Locations on Election Day 🚨  Governor Gavin Newsom enacts a dedicated buffer zone designed to insulate voters from intimidation at the ballot box.  Key takeaways from the signed measure:The Legislative Buffer: California Governor Gavin Newsom formally signed a statute that criminalizes or bars law enforcement arrests within 200 feet of any voting site on Election Day.  Addressing Voter Intimidation: The law aims to prevent operations by law enforcement or immigration agencies (such as ICE) near voting precincts that could deter eligible citizens from turning out.  Visual Flashpoint: Viral posts juxtaposed Newsom against tactical agents wearing "POLICE ICE" gear, framing the legislation as a shield for vulnerable and immigrant communities against aggressive enforcement.  The National Debate: Voting rights advocates celebrate the rule as a vital safeguard ensuring unimpeded civic participation, whereas conservative critics argue that restricting law enforcement jurisdiction near public buildings could hinder response efforts during genuine criminal activity. 💬 Do you view this 200-foot buffer as a necessary protection against voter intimidation, or does it limit law enforcement too broadly? Let us know below!#GavinNewsom #California #VotingRights #ElectionDay #ICE #PollingPlace #VoterProtection #ElectionIntegrity #USPolitics #BreakingNews #Trending

item.caption:
🗳️ I VOTED! ❤️🤍💙

Voting is more than just choosing candidates. It’s also about making decisions that directly impact our communities, schools, and future generations!

One important item on the DeKalb County ballot is the E-SPLOST referendum, which asks voters whether to renew the existing 1% education sales tax to help fund school renovations, technology, transportation, and facility improvements.

As an educator, I know firsthand how important it is for our students and teachers to have access to safe, updated, and well-equipped learning environments. 📚🏫

Don’t just vote for the people on the ballot—pay attention to the questions on the ballot, too! Take time to read, research, and make your voice heard.

🗳️ Get out and VOTE! Your voice matters!

#IVoted #DeKalbCounty #GeorgiaVotes #EducationMatters #YourVoteMatters

item.caption:
🇺🇸🗳️ TOMORROW IS THE DAY! EARLY VOTING STARTS MONDAY, OCTOBER 19!

Hey, my people in Marlboro, Chesterfield, and Richland Counties! ❤️💙🤍 It’s time to make a plan and make our voices heard!

I’m inviting YOU to join me on DAY 1 of Early Voting! Let’s start strong, exercise our right to vote, and encourage our family, friends, neighbors, and coworkers to participate in the democratic process.

📍 FIND YOUR COUNTY’S EARLY VOTING LOCATION:
👉 https://scvotes.gov/voters/early-voting/

🗳️ VIEW YOUR SAMPLE BALLOT:
Know what’s on your ballot before you go!
👉 https://vrems.scvotes.sc.gov/Voter/Login?PageMode=Sampleballot

📣 HERE’S YOUR CHALLENGE!
1️⃣ Make a plan to vote tomorrow!
2️⃣ Tag 3 people and invite them to join you.
3️⃣ After you vote, come back and comment “I VOTED!” or share your voting selfie! 📸
4️⃣ Encourage 3 more people to make their plan to vote!

Let’s turn one vote into a wave of civic participation across our communities!

Marlboro! Chesterfield! Richland! Are you ready? 🙋🏽‍♀️🙋🏾‍♂️

I’m planning to be there on DAY 1! Who’s joining me? Drop a 🗳️ in the comments!

Your vote is your voice. Make a plan, get informed, and participate!

#EarlyVoting2026 #MarlboroCounty #ChesterfieldCounty #RichlandCounty #IVoted #YourVoiceYourVote #NewSC #ShareThisPost

Jermaine Johnson For South Carolina Marlboro County for Dr. Johnson for SCMarlboro County Democratic Party@

#greenscreenvideo The 2026 midterms are two weeks away, and the warning signs are already here. Reporting shows pressure on state and local election officials, renewed fraud allegations, voter-roll scrutiny, and fears that chaos could be used to delay or challenge election results.
That does not mean the outcome is predetermined. It means voters need to be prepared: verify your registration, make a plan to vote, rely on your local election office for accurate information, and do not amplify unverified claims online.
A lie can circle the world before the truth has time to put its shoes on. Don’t let fear and misinformation keep you from voting.
#MidtermElections #ElectionIntegrity #VotingRights #TrumpNews

item.caption:
Countdown (Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3, which is 19 days from today)

19 days until Election Day. Don’t wait until November 3rd to find out there’s a problem. Do these 3 things NOW:

✅ 1. Check your voter status. Make sure you have not been purged and that ALL of your information is correct.

✅ 2. Call your local elections office. Confirm your ballot has gone out, and confirm your polling location.

✅ 3. Drive by your polling location before Election Day. Get a look at it so you can plan your day, including a plan for long lines and parking. We recommend taking @Uber or @Lyft to vote.

Your vote only counts if you can cast it. Plan ahead. 🗳️

#ElectionDay #Vote2026 #CheckYourRegistration #VoteReady #MidtermElections

author: elevatetheatrecompany

item.caption:
Happy Motivation Monday! 💪

Why does your vote matter on Election Day? Because civic action and community health go hand-in-hand. 🗳️✨

Did you know?
📊 4x More Engaged: According to research from the National Endowment for the Arts, people who participate in the arts were nearly 4 times as likely to engage civically in one national survey analysis.
🏥 Healthier Communities: Public health research explores connections between civic participation, social trust, and community well-being.

At Elevate, we use storytelling to create space for connection, understanding, and conversations about health. But how can we build stronger communities if people don't have opportunities to participate?

We need more accessible arts opportunities to bring people together, encourage civic participation, and help communities feel heard and represented. 🎭💙

By investing in the arts, we can create more spaces for people to share their stories, connect with others, and engage with the issues that shape their lives.

Your Election Day Checklist:
✅ Verify your voting site and opening hours.
✅ Read up on local ballot measures affecting healthcare and community arts.
✅ Check in on a neighbor or friend and help them make a voting plan!
Your story matters. Your health matters. And your voice matters. Let’s elevate our communities together! 💪🎭
👇 Drop a 🗳️ in the comments if you have your voting plan ready!

#MotivationMonday #ElevateTheatre #TheatreForHealth #CivicEngagement #ElectionDay #ArtsAndHealth #CommunityCare #MentalHealthMatters #UseYourVoice #PublicHealth #Elevate

item.caption:
✅ Hey you! Yes, you! Get out to the polls after work today, tomorrow, sometime this week! Early Voting starts today in Orange, Miami-Dade, Volusia, Putnam, Lee, and Indian River Counties (along with others).

👉 Why vote early? 
- It's more convenient: vote at ANY location in your county!
- Skip the lines: no need to wait in line for HOURS on Election Day (and there WILL be a line on Nov 3rd; it's the Midterms!) 
- Emergencies can come up unexpectedly, and you might miss the deadline on Election Day. Some things are too important to miss, so why not be ahead of schedule? 

Just so you know, the last day to register for a mail-in ballot is Thursday, Oct 22. Save yourself the stress and vote early! Want more information on the midterm elections? Check out your county's election website for more, or check out our upcoming Coffee Crawl!

#vote #vota #electionday

Vote NO on Amendment 3! 🗳️

In case you haven’t heard, Amendment 3 is too good to be true. Though it promises tax relief, it would shift the tax burden onto our most vulnerable people and take away essential services. To cover the financial loss Amendment 3 would create, agencies would need to find costs elsewhere, potentially through drastic cuts that would be exacerbated in lower-income communities.

🔗 If you'd like to learn more about Amendment 3, visit https://sosfl.org/

item.caption:
New Hampshire's Secretary of State asked the Supreme Court to bar poll workers from even considering a college student's ID on Nov. 3. Two federal courts have already said no to pausing the order against that directive.

The state says it's too late to retrain officials. A federal judge found the directive served no interest beyond those already served by the state's ID law. An expert for the voters' group estimated about 7,747 young New Hampshire citizens lack a qualifying ID, according to the court record.

Full story at the link in our bio.

author: italiareportusa

item.caption:
Per un italiano abituato a raggiungere il seggio nei giorni stabiliti per una consultazione, il sistema americano può apparire insolito. Infatti, quando arriva l’Election Day, una gran parte degli elettori ha già votato, perchè negli Stati Uniti, la partecipazione al voto può distribuirsi su diverse settimane, attraverso modalità disciplinate dai singoli Stati.

In Florida le possibilità sono tre: votare personalmente in anticipo, richiedere una scheda da compilare a casa e restituire il plico in persona presso uno dei seggi allestiti o per posta, oppure presentarsi al seggio nel giorno delle elezioni. Anche il voto anticipato, dunque si svolge in presenza.

Questa flessibilità consente di organizzarsi intorno agli impegni quotidiani. Chi lavora su turni, assiste un familiare o prevede di essere fuori città il 3 novembre può scegliere un’altra giornata, senza dover concentrare tutto nell’appuntamento conclusivo.

L'articolo completo su italiareportusa.com.

#florida #miami #usa #electionday #politics

item.caption:
Gen Z for @sherrod 🤝 Millennial for @sherrod 

The first Gen Z Congressman, @maxwellfrostfl, is in Ohio to do THE WORK! Not sure what I was expecting, meeting this renowned organizer & history maker, but consider me impressed & dare I say HOPEFUL! 

This election & all elections are about teamwork. You can’t just vote for President every 4 years. You vote in every election for candidates up & down the ballot. We can’t be #nokings while ignoring all the offices we vote on that are vital to our democracy. 

I can’t stop thinking about Congressman Frost’s work back home in Orlando - how it shapes a city & our country. I’m so grateful for his Ohio connection (shout out @tbdbitl & @wrightstateu) & that he cares enough to invest time in us. 

We get what we’re willing to fight for & it’s all hands on deck. 15 days until #electionday 🇺🇸

#vote #yayforburriss #bigburrissenergy

item.caption:
KNOW BEFORE YOU GO: Voting Checklist

If you’re heading to the polls, take a moment to prepare before you go!

A few reminders to help make your voting experience as smooth as possible:

✅ Bring your photo ID. Make sure you have an acceptable form of identification with you.

✅ Know your ballot. Take a few minutes to review your sample ballot before arriving so you know what to expect.

✅ Double-check your ballot. Before making your selections, take a moment to confirm that the ballot you receive matches your voting location and the election you’re there to vote in. If something doesn’t look right, ask an election official for assistance before proceeding.

✅ Take your time. Review your selections carefully before submitting your ballot.

Your voice matters, and every voter deserves the opportunity to cast their ballot accurately and confidently.

Thank you for being an engaged part of our community. 🇺🇸

#KnowBeforeYouGo #ColumbiaTN #MauryCounty #ElectionDay

⏰¡Oye, TÚ! Sí, TÚ! Vayaté a las urnas después del trabajo hoy, mañana, o un otro tiempo esta semana! La VOTACIÓN ANTICIPADA empieza hoy en los condados de Orange, Miami-Dade, Volusia, Putnam, Lee, and Indian River (y otros también).

- Es más conveniente: ¡vota en CUALQUIER ubicación en tu condado! 
- Evita las colas: no necesitas esperar en una colaboración por HORAS el día de Elecciones (y sí, estarán COLAS el 3 de noviembre; son las elecciones midterms!)

Hoy voté con el corazón, pensando en mi gente latina y en tantas familias que viven con miedo e incertidumbre.

item.caption:
We had a lot running around today bringing finds into @blacksheeppickersbwk, but we made sure to make time to vote. It was Day 6 of early voting for the November 3rd 2026 General Elections, and only 9,250 out of 62,340 eligible Glynn County Voters have showed up so far, just 14.8% of the voting population. But that’s okay, you still have time to exercise your right to vote.

Early voting runs through October 30, and then you have Election Day itself on November 3rd. Don’t know when, where or how to vote? Then just Google Glynn County Board of Elections and Registration, or go to their physical location at 1709 Gloucester Street in beautiful @discoverbrunswick to find out everything you need to know 🇺🇸🇺🇸🇺🇸

item.caption:
Make Your Voice Heard on November 3!

The statewide general election is Tuesday, November 3. San Mateo County has delivered vote-by-mail ballots, and today, Monday, October 19, is the deadline to register or update your voter information. If you miss today’s deadline, you can still register and vote in person at a county vote center through Election Day. Visit smccd.edu/registertovote to register, check your status and find other voting resources.

This year’s San Mateo County ballot includes Measure V, a bond measure placed on the ballot by the San Mateo County Community College District Board of Trustees. To learn what the measure includes and how it would be used, visit smccd.edu/futurefunding.

You can return completed ballots at an official ballot drop box at any of the three campuses through 8 p.m. on Election Day. Drop boxes are available at Cañada College in Parking Lot 4, College of San Mateo in Parking Lot A, and Skyline College in the median by Parking Lot N.

#CañadaCollege #SMCCD #ElectionDay #SanMateoCounty

Last call. Today is the final day to register to vote for the November 3rd election.

author: museumbanksy

item.caption:
Has humanity truly evolved, or have we simply built more elaborate institutions to disguise our primitive instincts?

Speaking of evolution and moving on, to everyone in the US, Election Day is coming up on November 3rd! Don't forget to check your voter registration and make a plan to vote.

In honor of the upcoming election, we're highlighting *Devolved Parliament* (2009), one of Banksy's most ambitious large-scale oil paintings.

Depicting the British House of Commons populated entirely by chimpanzees, the monumental work satirizes political authority, institutional dysfunction, and the illusion of civilized governance. Rather than destroying Parliament, the chimpanzees appear to conduct business as usual, suggesting that the absurdity may lie as much within the institution as with those who occupy it.

#Banksy #DevolvedParliament #arthistory #oilpainting #ElectionDay

Today was my first time experiencing a truly seamless voting process. No noise, no overwhelming crowds—just walk in, vote, and walk out.

Seeing how quiet, easy, and calm it was today makes me really pray that my home country can adopt this level of organization in the future.

author: hectormendeztx

item.caption:
I went out to vote on the very first day of early voting here in San Antonio, and what I thought would be a relatively quick trip turned into nearly FOUR HOURS of waiting in line near Northwest Vista College.

I’m glad I got to cast my ballot, but there’s no reason voting should take that long. We should be making it easier for Texans to vote, especially when so many people have jobs and other responsibilities that make waiting in line for hours difficult.

As I say every election year, I always encourage everyone to do their own research on the candidates and issues on the ballot. Take some time to look into who’s running, what they believe in, and what they’re actually proposing to do if elected.

Of course, as your CD 20 representative on the State Democratic Executive Committee, I’m proudly supporting Democrats up and down the ballot this November! I’m especially proud to have cast my vote for Clayton Tucker for Texas Agriculture Commissioner. As someone who currently works on his campaign’s communications, I’ve gotten to see firsthand how hard he works and how committed he is to fighting for everyday Texans. I’m proud to be part of his team and even prouder to have voted for him!

Early voting is underway, y’all! Make a plan to vote, check the wait times at your polling location if they’re available, and don’t forget to bring a little patience with you!

#IVoted #TexasVotes #EarlyVoting #TexasDemocrats #Election2026

item.caption:
✨🗳️ Our voices matter. Our stories matter. Our votes matter. 🗳️✨

As we approach Early Voting and Election Day, WOMAN (*Women of Minorities Achieving Now*) invites you to join us for a meaningful conversation about the power of using our voices to create change.

We are honored to welcome UNCP alumna Brittany Best** as our guest speaker. Brittany will share an inspiring and impactful message about why voting is so important, especially for communities whose voices have often been overlooked or underrepresented.

Voting is more than checking a box. It’s about showing up for ourselves, our families, our futures, and our communities. Every vote tells a story, and every voice deserves to be heard.

❤️ This event is open to everyone and all students are encouraged to attend. Whether this is your first election season or you’ve voted before, we welcome you to come learn, engage, and be part of the conversation.

Come be inspired, empowered, and reminded that your voice has power and your vote has purpose. @bretana__

🗳️ 15 days until Election Day!

This year, California voters will decide races for Governor and other statewide constitutional offices, 52 U.S. House seats, 20 State Senate seats, 80 State Assembly seats, judicial offices, and 14 statewide propositions, plus local candidates and measures that vary by community. 

These decisions can affect you, your family, and your community. Be informed. Be prepared. Make your vote count.

🗳️ Early voting and vote-by-mail options are available before Election Day.

item.caption:
🇺🇸 I DID MY PART — I VOTED EARLY! 🗳️

Today, I’m proud to say that I got out and voted early! 🇺🇸❤️🤍💙

Your vote is your voice. No matter what party you support or who you vote for, every eligible voter has the opportunity to help shape the future of our country, our state, and our communities.

Too many people say their vote doesn’t matter. But if it didn’t matter, why would we have the right to vote?

Our freedoms and our future are worth taking a few minutes out of our day. Don't sit on the sidelines and complain about things you have the opportunity to help change.

✅ Make your voice heard.
🗳️ Make a plan to vote.
🇺🇸 Encourage your family and friends to vote, too.

You don't have to agree with everyone else's choices. That's what makes our country special. We can have different opinions and still respect one another.

I did my part. Have you done yours?

👇 Drop a 🇺🇸 in the comments if you've voted, or share this post to encourage someone else to get out and vote!

#IVoted #YourVoteMatters #MakeYourVoiceHeard #GetOutAndVote #AmericanPride 🇺🇸

item.caption:
#ivoted today!

Well, mostly Friday, and finished yesterday - this California ballot was a bit of a beast, but so many important issues (and so much disinformation to sort through!) #votebymail is the best - plenty of time to research and no waiting in lines. Sill, so glad to be done!

I was wearing my “I voted” sticker at the grocery store and the cashier asked if I had early voted in person, and if so, where - so I looked it up. #alamedacounty early voting starts at a some locations on Saturday (2 polling places here in #berkeleyca ) and at all(?) polling locations 4 days early - so, on Halloween, I guess. Can’t wait to see all the costumes lined up to #vote !

author: conversations.in.color

item.caption:
Know what’s on your ballot and show up.

In 1940, Lonnie E. Smith, a Black dentist from Houston, Texas, was denied the right to vote in a Democratic primary because of his race. Four years later, on July 22, 1944, he cast his ballot in the Texas Democratic primary, just months after winning the landmark Supreme Court case Smith v. Allwright, which struck down the state's racially discriminatory white primary system.

#Vote2026 #ElectionDay #BlackVoters #BlackHistory #VotingRights #YourVoteMatters #CivicEngagement #BlackVoices

author: pbsintlpres35

item.caption:
Yesterday, I proudly exercised my right to vote! 🇺🇸🗳️

I never want to take this privilege for granted. When I think about the sacrifices so many people made to secure the right to vote, I’m reminded that this is more than just a trip to the polls—it’s an opportunity to make our voices heard and help shape the future of our families, our communities, and our country.

My late fraternity Brother, Hon. Congressman John Lewis said it best: “The vote is the most powerful nonviolent tool we have.” Those words carry a powerful message and a responsibility for each of us. We honor that legacy not only by remembering those who fought for this right, but by exercising it.

My encouragement to everyone who is eligible to vote: Make your voice heard! Take the time to learn about the issues, make an informed decision, and participate in the process. No matter your background or perspective, your voice deserves to be heard, and your participation matters.

Let’s never underestimate what we can accomplish when we show up, engage, and make our voices count. Democracy is stronger when we all participate! 🇺🇸

#IVoted #YourVoiceMatters #EveryVoiceCounts #CivicResponsibility #ConsciousCorporateLeader

author: disabilityrightsca

item.caption:
A federal court has ruled that California’s Vote-by-Mail Program violates the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, and California Government Code section 11135. The court held that the Vote-by-Mail Program discriminates against blind voters and others with print disabilities by forcing them to depend on another person to return their ballots. @dralegal 

Learn more and check out the full press release at the link in our bio.

The Court held that meaningful access to vote by mail includes the right to vote privately and independently. It pointed to the California Constitution’s command that “voting shall be secret” and found that requiring help from another person “is antithetical to voting in secret.” The Court rejected the Secretary of State’s argument that voters’ right to choose an assistant was enough, explaining that being allowed to have help is very different from being required to have it. 

“I’ve been voting for years, and I’ve never once cast a truly private ballot. That’s not because I can’t make my own choices. It’s because the State’s system doesn’t let me finish the job myself. This decision is a step toward changing that,” said Russell Dawson Rawlings, a voter with a mobility disability and named plaintiff. @rollingleft_foot 

#DisabilityRightsCA #CaliforniaCouncilOfTheBlind #CaliforniaVote #ElectionDay #ADA 
.
.

- Graphic 1: Three logos above for DRC, Disability Rights Advocates, and Brown Goldstein & Levy. Header Text: Press Release. Title Text: Federal Court Rules California Vote-by-Mail Program Discriminates Against Class of Voters with Print Disabilities. Blue filtered photo below of a person mailing out their ballot by dropping it in a mailbox.

- Graphic 2: Same logos. Quote Text: "Blind Californians have waited too long to cast a ballot that is truly our own. Every other voter marks a ballot, seals it, and sends it off without anyone looking over their shoulder. Today the court said we deserve exactly the same. - Guillermo Robles, President of California Council of the Blind. Circled text: Read the full press release at the link.

item.caption:
Стив Хилтон — это просто дитя Кремниевой долины. Это прямо эталонная эволюция tech spouse, только на максималках. 😂

Пока обычные переехавшие половинки открывают студии керамики, пекут тартин на закваске или ведут блог о том, как тяжело привыкнуть к местному кефиру, этот чувак пошёл по хардкору: искал себя, искал — и нашёл в кандидатах на губернаторское кресло пятой экономики мира.

Причём самое прекрасное в этой истории — жена. Рейчел Уэтстоун — влиятельнейший топ-менеджер по коммуникациям в Кремниевой долине. Google, Uber, Netflix. Семья переехала в Калифорнию в 2012 году. Жена пашет на руководящих должностях в бигтехе, а он такой: «Дорогая, я тут подумал… Керамика — это мелко. Пойду-ка я разберусь с налогами и бездомными в Сакраменто».

Но самое интересное — его политическая эволюция. В 2000-х в Лондоне Хилтон был одним из главных идеологов «либерального консерватизма». Убеждал Дэвида Кэмерона сделать британских консерваторов современными, экологичными и социально-либеральными. В британской прессе его тогда считали чуть ли не тайным левоцентристом. Хотя тут ещё вопрос политической географии: то, что в Великобритании считается умеренным левоцентризмом, в американских политических баталиях запросто могут записать в крайне правые 😅. Переехал в другую страну — и твои политические координаты уже пересчитали по местному курсу.

А теперь перед нами сторонник Трампа, бывший ведущий Fox News и кандидат в губернаторы Калифорнии от республиканцев. Вот это я понимаю — transferable skills. Вот это адаптация к американскому рынку труда. И после этого кто-то ещё будет говорить, что опыт работы в другой стране невозможно применить в США?

#сакраменто #калифорния #выборы2026 #stevehilton

item.caption:
Apollo: Did my civic duty today.  Dropped off my ballot, but disappointed with the limited choices.  Couldn't find the PAWfect candidate.  I mean is it that hard to make large green spaces dog friendly? What about a pawpool?  My cousin is senior & water therapy would be great for him.  My family feeds me the best of the best.  They deserve tax deductions for dog food & treats.  I know annual check ups are a necessary evils, but maybe I'd be more willing to go if you offered free medical & dental coverage.  Just saying...these pearly white are cheap.  I work hard for not only my humans, but I contribute a lot to my community.  I make my rounds everyday to share my love.  I pay my dues without you asking, but I'm not getting the services.  Is it too late to put my name on the ballot? 🤔🤭

item.caption:
PRE-ELECTION DAY PRAYER CIRCLES WITH KATHIANNE

Feeling some election jitters? You’re certainly not alone.

In the Sundays leading up to Election Day, join Kathianne Lewis, DD for a brief Prayer Circle - a sacred opportunity to step away from the noise, quiet the mind, reconnect with Spirit, and experience the healing power of praying together.
Whatever you may be feeling - anxiety, uncertainty, hope, concern, or simply the weight of this moment - come as you are. Together, we’ll create a space for peace, presence, connection, and prayer.

Sundays, October 25 & November 1, 10:20–10:40 a.m. & 12:20–12:40 p.m.
In Person: Sanctuary
Online: Zoom : https://bit.ly/4z03Nln

Please note: The in-person and online gatherings are separate prayer circles, rather than a hybrid experience.
Come for twenty minutes. Breathe. Pray. Remember that peace is still possible - and that we can help bring it into the world.

Pray Up. Show up. Vote.

item.caption:
**CARVILLE: RATHER REPUBLICANS KEEP POWER THAN DEMOCRATS WIN HOUSE OR SENATE**

James Carville said the quiet part out loud.

The architect of the Clinton machine — the veteran Democratic strategist who the party still trots out as its wise old man — went on  and declared he would rather see Republicans keep the House by 5 seats than see Democrats win it by 5.

Why? Because a Democratic win would leave his own party "hostage to the DSA."

Let that sink in. A lifelong Democrat would rather have Speaker  gaveling in a Republican majority than have  held accountable by the actual grassroots of his party.

This isn't a gaffe. This is the Democrats' civil war in plain view. In our prior article on the Democrats' family divide, we laid out how the moderate consultant class and the DSA-progressive wing are fighting for control of the big tent. Carville just proved it.

He didn't stop at the House. He said a close Senate would have  keeping  on "Pepto-Bismol all night." Translation: the moderate wing can't stand its own senators, its own voters, or its own future.

Moderate strategist Kaivan Shroff tried to clean it up, calling Carville "absolutely wrong" and "irresponsible" and whining that it gives ammunition to the far left and discourages Democrats from showing up. Shroff is right about one thing — it DOES discourage Democrats from showing up. Because when voters hear that Carville Democrats hate DSA Democrats more than they hate MAGA, they believe it.

This is no longer policy disagreement. This is contempt. The Clinton wing would rather lose to Trump-aligned Republicans than share power with  and the progressive left they helped create.

The Democrats' family is more divided in its big tent than ever before, and the feud has moved out of the  Ring and into the front row seats!

author: network_nova

item.caption:
AMERICA ON THE LINE: The Midterms, Our Rights & What Comes Next

Friday Power Lunch, Oct 23, 12–1 PM ET

We are just 11 days from #ElectionDay, and America is coming into the final stretch with a lot on the line.

Virginia is at the center of the fight for control of Congress. Three constitutional amendments are on our ballot. Health care, reproductive freedom and voting rights are under pressure. Immigration enforcement is changing daily life in communities across Virginia. And beyond our borders, questions about Ukraine, Russia and America’s role in the world are getting louder.

This Friday, we go from the national picture straight to what all of this means on the ground.

U.S. Rep. Jennifer McClellan (VA-04) joins us with a view from Congress and the campaign trail. She has been traveling across Virginia supporting competitive congressional races, campaigning for Virginia’s constitutional amendments, speaking out about health-care cuts and maternal health, and defending voting and reproductive rights. We’ll ask what she is seeing in these final days and what she believes Americans should be paying attention to now. https://mcclellan.house.gov/

John Cano, Senior Supervising Organizer with the Legal Aid Justice Center, brings us into Virginia communities where debates over immigration and federal enforcement are very real. John works with immigrant and working families on Know Your Rights education, civic engagement and access to justice, and will help us understand what families are experiencing right now and the major legal fights ahead. https://www.justice4all.org/staff/john-cano/

Eleven days. A country in motion. And a lot to talk about.

#ConstitutionalAmendments #ReproductiveRights #MarriageEquality #VotingRights #KnowYourRights #Midterms #Elections #Immigration #LegalAidJusticeCenter #Vote #VoteEarly #VirginiaGrassroots #GrassrootsGetItDone #NetworkNOVA #FridayPowerLunch

Early voting is in full swing! Here's a quick checklist of things to get you prepped. And remember, if you're someone who can't wait in a long line due to a health condition, go to the front and talk to the poll workers to explain your situation and they can accomodate you!

- Check your voter registration
- Find your polling place
- Review your ballot
- Download our Let The People Judge nonpartisan guide (link in bio) and get informed on the courts. You can even print out this guide or take handwritten notes into the polling place, just make sure you don't leave them inside - take them out with you! 

Happy voting everyone!

author: robadadonne

item.caption:
Finora se ne è parlato veramente poco...
Ma cosa rischia davvero Donald Trump se perde la maggioranza al Congresso? 🇺🇸👇

Le elezioni di Midterm non sono un semplice appuntamento elettorale di routine: sono il vero “termometro” della democrazia americana e il principale contrappeso al potere della Casa Bianca.

Ogni quattro anni, a metà mandato presidenziale, i cittadini americani tornano alle urne per ridefinire gli equilibri a Washington. Anche se la carica del Presidente non è in discussione fino al 2029, gli esiti di questo voto possono trasformare radicalmente i suoi ultimi due anni di governo.

Dallo stallo legislativo (la celebre condizione di “anatra zoppa”) al controllo sul bilancio federale, fino all’avvio di commissioni d’inchiesta e al blocco delle nomine dei giudici della Corte Suprema: una vittoria dell’opposizione può frenare quasi del tutto l’agenda politica del Presidente.

Abbiamo analizzato nel dettaglio come funzionano Camera e Senato, i dati storici dal dopoguerra a oggi e tutti gli scenari possibili.

💬 Cosa ne pensi? Il Presidente riuscirà a mantenere la maggioranza dopo la campagna elettorale di queste settimane o assisteremo a un ribaltamento? Scrivilo nei commenti👇🏻
#elezionimidterm2026 #donaldtrump #casabianca #attualità #usa🇺🇸 

Immagine Donald Trump: credits @pixabay - autore - heblo

Il sistema istituzionale statunitense adotta le Midterm come strumento di equilibrio costituzionale tra il potere esecutivo e quello legislativo.

#politica #affariesteri #elezioniusa 

Oltre al Congresso federale, il voto coinvolge contemporaneamente l’elezione dei governatori in 36 Stati americani.

#dirittoalvoto #voto #america 

Rinnovandosi per intero ogni due anni, la Camera dei Rappresentanti riflette fedelmente gli sbalzi di consenso dell’opinione pubblica.

#congresso #electionday 

Il rinnovo parziale del Senato assicura stabilità diplomatica e continuità istituzionale durante i cambi di amministrazione.

#senato #politica #politicaestera 

Gli attuali equilibri d’aula rendono decisivo ogni singolo seggio per la maggioranza al Congresso.

#equilibrio #repubblicani #democratici

imageDescriptions: An illustration depicts a politician with blonde hair and a suit, raising a fist. Two American flags are shown in the upper right corner, and text in blue and red is visible. Below the politician, a silhouette of the Statue of Liberty and a megaphone are also illustrated.

A graphic with the text "CHE COSA SONO LE ELEZIONI DI MIDTERM?" is displayed. Below this, further text explains that these elections balance presidential power and check popular consent. Two American flags are depicted on the left.

The image displays text asking "MA COSA SI VOTA?". Below this are three boxes detailing different voting categories: 435 seats in the Chamber, 35 seats in the Senate, and 36 Governors. The image also shows "QUANDO SI VOTA? 03 NOVEMBRE 2026" in large text.

The image contains text on a light blue background. A graphic of a hand holding a pen is in the upper right corner. Text in large, dark blue sans-serif font asks "LE RAGIONI PRINCIPALI DI QUESTO VOTO?". Below this, in red capital letters, is "1) RINNOVO DELLA CAMERA DEI DEPUTATI". Smaller blue text explains the term of deputies.

item.caption:
I VOTED! DID YOU? 🇺🇸🗳️

Today, I dropped off my ballot here in Sonoma County! Did you?!?!

I had the privilege of serving in elected office then I lost my reelection by a single vote. Just one. So when I say EVERY. SINGLE. VOTE. MATTERS., believe me, I know what I’m talking about!

Voting is more than just a civic responsibility. It’s an opportunity to make our voices heard, stand up for what we believe in, and help shape the future of our communities.

Regardless of your political affiliation or who you support, I encourage you to take the time to research the issues, make informed decisions, and most importantly, participate in our democracy.

I’ve done my part. 
Now it’s your turn!

Your voice matters. Your vote matters. YOU matter! ❤️🤍💙

item.caption:
There is no federal law that gives you time off to vote. Your state might.

The Center for American Progress counts 20 states plus D.C. with paid voting leave, and eight more that require unpaid time or a schedule change. In California, you can get up to two hours of paid time if you don't have enough time outside work, with at least two working days' notice.

Our story covers seven big states and what to do before Nov. 3. Ask in writing, and ask now.

Full story at the link in our bio.

What is on the ballot for the @bourbonnaispubliclibrary this election? 

 In the latest WVLI News Update Special Report, host @jakelamoremedia is joined by Jeremy Van Kley from the Vote Yes for Bourbonnais Public Library committee to review the upcoming funding referendum on the November 3 ballot. 

Key discussion points include:

- Details on the proposed tax rate adjustment and how it is calculated 

- District boundaries and eligibility for area voters, including renters 

- Projected building maintenance, collection expansions, and facility updates 

- Early voting locations and election information 

Get all the facts before casting your vote. Listen to the full interview on our website or wherever podcasts are found.

item.caption:
Two years ago Michigan introduced a design contest for its "I Voted" stickers - and it became so popular that this year there were over 2,000 entries, more than four times greater than the first time around. The choices are narrowed down by the Collegiate Student Advisory Task Force to 30 in each of three categories (general, high-school, and under-12), and then the general public voted online to determine three winners in each category. @DeltaCollege student Justin Evans, who served on that advisory board, talked about how helpful this contest can be in a story by Berl Schwartz for @MichiganPublic Media.

A little midterm election reminder!

Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, 2026!

I know life is life-ing right now! Between work, family, responsibilities, and everything else, it's easy for important dates to sneak up on us.

So here's your friendly reminder to review who's on your ballot, research the candidates and issues, and make a plan for the midterms!

Whether you're voting early, by mail, or on 11/3, be sure you know the rules and deadlines in your state.

You can find voter information at Vote.gov.

That's it! That's the reminder! 

Have you checked your voting plan yet?

#MidtermElections2026 #CivicEngagement #YourVoteYourVoice #ElectionDay #StayInformed

author: 1dopeprincipal

item.caption:
Listen… 👀🗳️

I’m not gonna tell you who to vote for, but I AM going to tell you to GO VOTE!

As an educator, public education is personal to me. The well-being of ALL children, the people who educate and care for ALL of them, and the opportunities we create for the next generation matter. Those things, along with other issues that directly impact my life and the lives of people I care about, influence my voting decisions — NOT political parties.

I believe in doing my research, asking questions, looking beyond the headlines, and paying attention to how decisions impact real people. I encourage you to do the same.

If you’ve never voted… VOTE!
If you’re uncertain, do your research and… VOTE!
If you’re registered and eligible… VOTE!
If you’ve got an excuse, reconsider it and… VOTE!

Your vote is your voice. Use it!

And listen… if we want things to change, we have to be willing to participate in the process. We can’t complain about decisions that impact our children, our schools, our families, and our future while refusing to show up when we have the opportunity to make our voices heard.

Don’t sit this one out. Be informed. Be intentional. Be part of the process. GO VOTE! 🗳️❤️📚

#IVoted #PublicEducationMatters #YourVoiceYourVote #BePartOfTheSolution

author: betaxi_aka

item.caption:
A new polling location, but the same opportunity to make your voice heard! 🗳️💚🩷

Due to recent changes, the local polling location has moved from the nearby Wilberforce University campus to Xenia Grace Chapel, approximately six miles away. While this means a slightly longer trip to the polls, transportation doesn’t have to stand in your way!

With support from the Ohio Black Legislative Caucus, free transportation is being made available to help Central State students get to the polls! 🚗

This is an opportunity to exercise your right to vote alongside your peers, come together as a campus community, and participate in shaping the future of our communities. Every voice matters, and yours deserves to be heard!

Need a ride? 📲 Scan the QR code and fill out the requested information to access transportation assistance. Be sure to make your plans ahead of Election Day!

Let’s show up, support one another, and make our voices count together! 💗✨

#AKA1908 #BetaXiChapter #CampusResources #YourVoteMatters #electionday

item.caption:
राम-राम सा / जय माता दी 🚩
ग्राम पंचायत पिचियाक के सभी देवतुल्य मतदाताओं, बुजुर्गों, माताओं-बहनों और युवा साथियों को सादर प्रणाम! 🙏

✨ “36 कौम का एक ही नारा, मंगला राम जी भाई हमारा!” ✨

पिचियाक ग्राम पंचायत के चहुंमुखी विकास, आपसी भाईचारे को मजबूत करने, हर वर्ग को न्याय दिलाने और एक पारदर्शी शासन की स्थापना के लिए सर्व समाज (36 कौम) की ओर से आप सभी से हाथ जोड़कर विनम्र निवेदन है:
आने वाली चुनाव की तारीख को अपने उज्जवल भविष्य और पिचियाक की तरक्की के लिए हमारे अपने, लोकप्रिय, कर्मठ, ईमानदार और प्रगतिशील सरपंच पद के उम्मीदवार श्री मंगला राम सीरवी जी को अपना अमूल्य वोट, समर्थन और आशीर्वाद देकर भारी मतों से विजयी बनाएं। 🗳️

हमारा संकल्प और उद्देश्य:
🔹 हर घर को स्वच्छ जल की आपूर्ति
🔹 पक्की सड़कें और उन्नत नालियों का निर्माण
🔹 बेहतर शिक्षा और स्वास्थ्य सुविधाएं
🔹 हर वर्ग का सम्मान और न्याय

यह चुनाव सिर्फ एक पद का नहीं, बल्कि हमारी पिचियाक पंचायत की खुशहाली और तरक्की का है। आपका एक-एक वोट पिचियाक के विकास का मजबूत आधार बनेगा।

निवेदक: सर्व समाज एवं 36 कौम, ग्राम पंचायत पिचियाक। 🤝

item.caption:
I am blown away by the breadth and creativity in the first round of this year's GRAMMY® Awards submissions. After several more hours of careful listening, I cast my votes today.

To my fellow Recording Academy members, your artistry is amazing! I know how much emotion, and how many hundreds of hours, late nights, and juggling of responsibilities goes into bringing these projects to life. It was particularly interesting listening to recordings and artists that were new to me - and now I have a bunch of new additions to my playlists.

To those who took the time to reach out via email and DMs, thank you for your patience as the wave of messages was a little overwhelming, and I wasn't always able to respond right away.

It's an honor to be a part of this community, and to listen to your creations. To all of the composers, instrumentalists, vocalists, ensembles, producers, and engineers involved, you deserve to be proud! 👏🏼

#GRAMMYS #fyc #recordingacademy #ivoted #musicianlife

item.caption:
12 Days left to vote!
 
Nevada, it’s time to make your voting plan! You’ve got options:

📬 Vote by mail: Fill out your ballot, sign the return envelope, and send it back. You can also drop it off at an official ballot drop box.

🏃🏽 Early vote in person: Stop by an early voting location between now and October 30.

📍 Vote on Election Day: Head to a voting location on Tuesday, November 3.

Your voice matters, and your vote is one way to make it heard. 💪🏽 Make a plan, check your ballot, and remind your relatives and friends to vote, too!

🔗 Find voting locations and check your registration at VOTE.NV.gov.

#NativeVoteNevada #NativeVote #ElectionDay #NativeVoicesMatter NevadaVotes

author: seanstinnett0541

item.caption:
🗳️ I VOTED TODAY!

Today, I proudly exercised my right to vote and cast my ballot YES on Question 3! Every time I vote, I reflect on the generations who marched, organized, and sacrificed to ensure that we could have a voice in our democracy.

As a Baltimore resident and your Delegate, voting is deeply personal to me. It is an opportunity to put my values into action and participate in shaping the future of our city and state. I’m grateful to everyone who worked to secure this right and to the election workers helping our communities make their voices heard.

Proud to have cast my ballot today!

Building A Stronger District….Together!!

#IVoted #YesOnQuestion3

item.caption:
Around 150,000 supporters of a student-led movement gathered in Belgrade in a final campaign rally ahead of Sunday’s Parliamentary election.

The Student List is threatening former President Aleksander Vučić’s 12 years in power, after he resigned in September and announced the snap vote.

The Student List does not have a leader, but its 250 candidates include university professors, actors, farmers and even a popular rapper.

Right-wing populist leader Vučić has served two terms as president and cannot seek a third, but he’s hoping to return to the post of Prime Minister, which he left in 2017.

#Serbia #Vučić #StudentList #C4News

item.caption:
Iron sharpens iron.

Proverbs 27:17 reminds us that we become better—stronger, wiser, more accountable—when we engage with one another. Voting is one of the clearest ways we do that in a free society. We sharpen our communities, our future, and each other by showing up and making our voices count.

Proud to have cast my ballot in the general election today.

Wearing the reminder on my chest (literally): Iron sharpens iron.

item.caption:
North Carolina, consider this your official reminder to pull up to the polls! 👀🗳️🔥 

Early voting is happening now, and the group chat needs to know! From Charlotte and Raleigh to Durham, Greensboro, Fayetteville, and communities across NC, the 2026 midterm elections are bringing attention to affordable housing, healthcare, education, Duke Energy bills, jobs, and the rising cost of living. Because the people making decisions in government can influence the issues affecting our everyday lives! 

NC early voting runs October 15–31, 2026, including some weekends, and Election Day is November 3. Make your voting plan today! Check your registration, research the candidates, review your sample ballot, and find your early voting location and hours at https://vt.ncsbe.gov/EVSite/. 

Not registered? Eligible NC residents can register and vote during the same early voting visit with acceptable photo ID and proof of current residential address. Learn more at https://www.ncsbe.gov/registering/how-register/register-person-during-early-voting. 

Tag your NC bestie, share this with the group chat, and tell us: Are you team early voting or team Election Day? 🗳️🔥 #TheCultureDecides

From Charlotte and Raleigh to Durham, Greensboro, Fayetteville, and communities across NC, the 2026 midterm elections are bringing attention to affordable housing, healthcare, education, Duke Energy bills, jobs, and the rising cost of living. Because the people making decisions in government can influence the issues affecting our everyday lives! 

NC early voting runs October 15–31, 2026, including some weekends, and Election Day is November 3. Make your voting plan today! Check your registration, research the candidates, review your sample ballot, and find your early voting location and hours at https://vt.ncsbe.gov/EVSite/. 

Not registered? Eligible NC residents can register and vote during the same early voting visit with acceptable photo ID and proof of current residential address. Learn more at https://www.ncsbe.gov/registering/how-register/register-person-during-early-voting. 

Tag your NC bestie, share this with the group chat, and tell us: Are you team early voting or team Election Day? 🗳️🔥 #TheCultureDecides

item.caption:
Election Day in Massachusetts is Tuesday, November 3, and the deadline to register is Saturday, October 24.

Register or update your registration at VoteInMA.com: online until 11:59 PM, or in person at your local election office by 5 PM.

Swipe for the dates to know what's on your ballot and where BECMA stands on Question 8.

Key dates:
Oct. 24: Last day to register or update your registration
Oct. 27: Vote-by-mail applications must reach your local election office by 5 PM
Oct. 30: Last day of early voting
Nov. 3: Election Day. Polls are open 7 AM–8 PM

This year's ballot has nine statewide questions. BECMA endorses a NO vote on Question 8, which would dismantle Massachusetts' recreational marijuana industry and wipe out Black-owned and social equity businesses that have fought for a foothold in it.

Before you vote, read the full questions and what a YES or NO vote means in the state's 2026 Information for Voters guide. Link in bio.

If you believe your right to vote has been violated, call the Secretary of the Commonwealth's Elections Division at 1-800-462-VOTE (8683).

Save this post and share it with your community.

#MApoli #ElectionDay #BECMA

Nov. 3: Election Day. Polls are open 7 AM–8 PM

This year's ballot has nine statewide questions. BECMA endorses a NO vote on Question 8, which would dismantle Massachusetts' recreational marijuana industry and wipe out Black-owned and social equity businesses that have fought for a foothold in it.

Before you vote, read the full questions and what a YES or NO vote means in the state's 2026 Information for Voters guide. Link in bio.

If you believe your right to vote has been violated, call the Secretary of the Commonwealth's Elections Division at 1-800-462-VOTE (8683).

Save this post and share it with your community.

item.caption:
The Kenosha General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Here is what you need to know before you vote. 🗳️

Polls are open from 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. Find your polling location at MyVote.WI.Gov or contact the City Clerk's Office directly.

Early in-person absentee voting is available at the Kenosha Municipal Building, 625 52nd Street, through Friday, October 30. Most days run 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with extended hours on select dates including until 7:00 p.m. on Wednesdays.

Preferring to vote by mail? The deadline to request a mail ballot is 5:00 p.m. on Thursday, October 29. Completed ballots must be received at the City Clerk's Office by 8:00 p.m. on November 3 — do not drop them at a polling location.

Photo ID is required to vote. Accepted forms include a Wisconsin driver license or ID, U.S. passport, U.S. military ID, or unexpired Veterans photo ID. Full list at BringIt.WI.Gov.

Get the complete voting guide — deadlines, hours, and more — at the link in bio:
